# Friction

> Friction is a dual usability laboratory for testing the same task through a visible human interface and page-owned WebMCP agent tools.

## Product

- Live app: https://friction.alx21.chatgpt.site/
- Source: https://github.com/agammann/friction-webmcp
- License: MIT
- Scenario: RelayConf event registration
- Parity dimensions: outcome, information, consent, state, and effort

## WebMCP tools

The top-level page registers ten imperative tools over the same visible browser state:

- get_test_scenario: read the active task, prices, conditions, and expected outcome
- start_agent_run: start a fresh structured agent trace
- inspect_task_state: read the shared scenario, draft, approval, and completion state
- configure_registration: select the supported ticket and quiet-zone seat
- review_registration: return the itemized total and issue a one-time review token
- complete_simulated_task: require the current review token and confirmed=true before completion
- get_human_interaction_trace: read the visible human journey and usability signals
- compare_human_agent_runs: compare outcome, information, consent, state, and effort
- submit_parity_finding: add an evidence-backed finding for visible human review
- propose_interface_patch: propose a change without approving or applying it

## Repaired workflow example

1. Call start_agent_run with an empty object.
2. Call configure_registration with ticket="general_admission" and seat_preference="quiet_zone".
3. Call review_registration and retain the returned one-time reviewToken.
4. Call complete_simulated_task with that reviewToken and confirmed=true.
5. Call compare_human_agent_runs to inspect the parity result.

## Safety boundary

Agents can submit findings and propose interface changes. Patch approval is deliberately available only through the visible human interface and is not exposed as a WebMCP tool.

## Updates

The live app and repository are the authoritative sources for current behavior.
